person_note: The controlling narrator is the fictional Philip Roth, participating in the story as a child while narrating retrospectively as an adult. Numerous event passages independently expose this first-person position through “I,” “we,” “my,” “me,” and “our,” and the official publisher guide plus two scholarly sources confirm the same structure across the novel. Third-person historical and neighborhood passages are expansions within that first-person account, not autonomous third-person sections. First-person pronouns confined to character speech were treated as local, while dialogue passages with narratorial beats such as “I asked” or “my father” still expose the base narrator. No credible evidence of sustained narration in another person was found; remaining uncertainty is negligible.
